Open one level at a time. **Hint 1** gives the conceptual direction, **Hint 2** the SQL technique, **Hint 3** the query structure, and the final level is in [`solutions/`](../solutions/).

## M4-E01 · Index the title column

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

An index is built on the column(s) your WHERE clause filters on.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`CREATE INDEX name ON table (column);`

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`CREATE INDEX "title_index" ON "movies" ("title");`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M4.md#m4-e01).

## M4-E02 · Which columns should be indexed for the Tom Hanks query?

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Read the plan from the innermost subquery outward. Which tables say SCAN?

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Index the column each WHERE clause filters on, `people.name` and `stars.person_id`.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`CREATE INDEX "person_index" ON "stars" ("person_id"); CREATE INDEX "name_index" ON "people" ("name");`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M4.md#m4-e02).

## M4-E03 · Make the stars index covering

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

A covering index contains every column the query reads from that table.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Drop the old index, then create it on (`person_id`, `movie_id`). The filter column comes first.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`DROP INDEX "person_index"; CREATE INDEX "person_index" ON "stars" ("person_id", "movie_id");`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M4.md#m4-e03).

## M4-E04 · A partial index for recent movies

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

A partial index is a normal CREATE INDEX with a WHERE clause at the end.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Only rows matching that WHERE are stored in the index, so it is smaller.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`CREATE INDEX "recents" ON "movies" ("title") WHERE "year" = 2023;`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M4.md#m4-e04).

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

## M4-E06 · Alice pays Bob $10, atomically

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Wrap both UPDATEs between `BEGIN TRANSACTION;` and `COMMIT;`

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Update relative to the current value: `SET "balance" = "balance" + 10`.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`BEGIN TRANSACTION; UPDATE "accounts" SET "balance" = "balance" + 10 WHERE "id" = 2; UPDATE ... - 10 WHERE "id" = 1; COMMIT;`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M4.md#m4-e06).

## M4-E07 · Roll back a transfer that breaks a constraint

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Credit Bob, then try to debit Alice. Which statement fails?

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

After a failure inside a transaction, the earlier statements are *still pending*, not undone.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`BEGIN TRANSACTION; UPDATE ... + 10 WHERE "id" = 2; UPDATE ... - 10 WHERE "id" = 1; ROLLBACK;`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M4.md#m4-e07).

## M4-E08 · Defuse the race condition

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

The danger is checking the balance in one step and spending it in a later step that runs concurrently.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Each transfer (check + credit + debit) must run as one isolated unit, one after another.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

Put the balance check and both updates in one transaction; the second transfer then sees $0 and rolls back.

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M4.md#m4-e08).

## M4-E09 · Lab: see an exclusive lock block a reader

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Which lock kinds exist in SQLite? Which one allows other readers?

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

EXCLUSIVE means nobody else may read or write.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

B gets an error until A ends its transaction.

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M4.md#m4-e09).

## M4-E10 · Lab: VACUUM gives space back

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

What does SQLite do with the pages an index used to occupy?

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

It marks them free for reuse and keeps them in the file.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

Only VACUUM rebuilds the file and returns those pages to the operating system.

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M4.md#m4-e10).

## M4-E12 · Walk the B-tree to find Turning Red

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

At each node, ask "does my value come before this key?" to pick the child to follow.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Turning Red comes after Frozen and after Soul, so which child does that leave?

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

Costs: think about pages in a printed book, and about where a new title has to be inserted.

</details>

## D4-01 · An index with the columns backwards

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

A multi-column index is sorted by its first column, then by the second.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

The query filters on `person_id`. Can a list sorted by movie_id be searched by person_id?

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

Put the filter column first, `("person_id", "movie_id")`.

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M4.md#d4-01).

## D4-02 · An index nobody uses

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Run EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on `SELECT * FROM "movies" WHERE "title" = 'Cars';`

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

An index only helps queries that filter (or sort) on its columns.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

Index `title`.

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M4.md#d4-02).

## D4-03 · A partial index that doesn't match the query

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

SQLite can use a partial index only when the query's WHERE implies the index's WHERE.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Does `year = 2023` imply `year = 2022`?

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

Make the index condition match the query.

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M4.md#d4-03).

## D4-04 · A transfer that created money

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Without a transaction, each statement commits on its own.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Group the two updates into one unit of work.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`BEGIN TRANSACTION;` … both updates … then `ROLLBACK;` after the failure.

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M4.md#d4-04).
